stele.t: Merneptah Stele ('Israel Stele'). Egyptian Museum, Cairo, JE 31408 / CG 34025. Granite; found by W. M. F. Petrie in 1896 in Merneptah's mortuary temple, western Thebes. Year 5 of Merneptah.

petrie1897.t: Petrie, W. M. F. (1897). Six Temples at Thebes, 1896. London: Quaritch.

kitchen4.t: Kitchen, K. A. (2003). Ramesside Inscriptions, Translated and Annotated. Translations, vol. IV: Merenptah and the Late Nineteenth Dynasty. Oxford: Blackwell. (Israel Stele; Great Karnak Inscription)

hasel.t: Hasel, M. G. (1994). 'Israel in the Merneptah Stela'. Bulletin of the American Schools of Oriental Research 296: 45–62.

bryce.t: Bryce, T. (2005). The Kingdom of the Hittites. New edition. Oxford University Press.

bryce2006.t: Bryce, T. (2006). 'The “Eternal Treaty” from the Hittite perspective'. British Museum Studies in Ancient Egypt and Sudan 6: 1–11.

beckman.t: Beckman, G. (1999). Hittite Diplomatic Texts. 2nd ed., ed. H. A. Hoffner Jr. SBL Writings from the Ancient World 7. Atlanta: Scholars Press. (incl. the Egyptian–Hittite treaty)

morris.t: Morris, E. F. (2005). The Architecture of Imperialism: Military Bases and the Evolution of Foreign Policy in Egypt's New Kingdom. Probleme der Ägyptologie 22. Leiden: Brill.

moran.t: Moran, W. L. (1992). The Amarna Letters. Baltimore: Johns Hopkins University Press. (letters 'EA', 14th century BC)

killebrew.t: Killebrew, A. E. (2005). Biblical Peoples and Ethnicity: An Archaeological Study of Egyptians, Canaanites, Philistines, and Early Israel, 1300–1100 B.C.E. Archaeology and Biblical Studies 9. Atlanta: SBL.

butzer.t: Butzer, K. W. (1976). Early Hydraulic Civilization in Egypt: A Study in Cultural Ecology. University of Chicago Press, pp. 80–87 (c. 2.9 million people around 1250 BC).

oconnor.t: Trigger, B. G., Kemp, B. J., O'Connor, D. & Lloyd, A. B. (1983). Ancient Egypt: A Social History. Cambridge University Press. (O'Connor: New Kingdom c. 2.9–4.5 million; cited via TheTorah.com summary)

during.t: Düring, B. S. (2020). The Imperialisation of Assyria: An Archaeological Approach. Cambridge University Press.

grayson.t: Grayson, A. K. (1987). Assyrian Rulers of the Third and Second Millennia BC (to 1115 BC). RIMA 1. University of Toronto Press. (Tukulti-Ninurta I inscriptions)

riao.t: Tukulti-Ninurta I, inscription 23 (RIMA 1 A.0.78.23): '28,800 Hittites' taken across the Euphrates. Online edition, ORACC RIAo.

chron.t: Chronicle of Tukulti-Ninurta I (Grayson ABC 22 / CM 13), translation on Livius.org.

brinkman.t: Brinkman, J. A. (1976). Materials and Studies for Kassite History, vol. 1: A Catalogue of Cuneiform Sources Pertaining to Specific Monarchs of the Kassite Dynasty. Chicago: Oriental Institute.

potts.t: Potts, D. T. (2016). The Archaeology of Elam: Formation and Transformation of an Ancient Iranian State. 2nd ed. Cambridge University Press.

finkelstein.t: Finkelstein, I. (1988). The Archaeology of the Israelite Settlement. Jerusalem: Israel Exploration Society.

fink2013.t: Finkelstein, I. (2013). The Forgotten Kingdom: The Archaeology and History of Northern Israel. Atlanta: SBL, pp. 22–23 (c. 30 sites / 50 ha in LB II; c. 250 sites / 220 ha in late Iron I).

faust.t: Faust, A. (2006). Israel's Ethnogenesis: Settlement, Interaction, Expansion and Resistance. London: Equinox.

kuhrt.t: Kuhrt, A. (1995). The Ancient Near East c. 3000–330 BC. 2 vols. London: Routledge.

vdm.t: Van De Mieroop, M. (2016). A History of the Ancient Near East ca. 3000–323 BC. 3rd ed. Wiley-Blackwell.

cline.t: Cline, E. H. (2021). 1177 B.C.: The Year Civilization Collapsed. Revised and updated ed. Princeton University Press.

yasur.t: Yasur-Landau, A. (2010). The Philistines and Aegean Migration at the End of the Late Bronze Age. Cambridge University Press.

garr.t: Garr, W. R. (1987). 'A Population Estimate of Ancient Ugarit'. BASOR 266: 31–43.

gilibert.t: Gilibert, A. (2021). 'Urban Squares in Late Bronze Age Ugarit: a Street View on Ancient Near Eastern Governance'. Journal of Near Eastern Studies 80(2).

schachner.t: Schachner, A. (2017). 'Hattusa and its Environs: Archaeology'. In M. Weeden & L. Z. Ullmann (eds), Hittite Landscape and Geography. Leiden: Brill, 37–49.

schachner2024.t: Schachner, A. (2024). 'A new look at an ancient city: An outline of the chronological and urban development of the Hittite capital Ḫattuša'. Anatolian Studies 74: 13–46.

zuckerman.t: Zuckerman, S. (2007). 'Anatomy of a Destruction: Crisis Architecture, Termination Rituals and the Fall of Canaanite Hazor'. Journal of Mediterranean Archaeology 20(1): 3–32.

fink2005.t: Finkelstein, I. (2005). 'Hazor at the End of the Late Bronze Age: A Reassessment'. Ugarit-Forschungen 37: 341–349.

abbas.t: Raafat Abbas, M. (2017). 'The Town of Yenoam in the Ramesside War Scenes and Texts of Karnak'. Cahiers de Karnak 16: 329–341.

soleb.t: Soleb temple of Amenhotep III (Sudan), toponym list: 'land of the Shasu, yhw'. Reading as the divine name Yahweh is disputed; summary with references.

aram.t: Oxford Bibliographies: 'Aram' (earliest undisputed mention of Arameans in inscriptions of Tiglath-pileser I, c. 1112 BC).

bible.t: Hebrew Bible: Exodus, Joshua, Judges. Religious tradition, written down centuries after 1200 BC.

ne.t: Natural Earth (public domain): coastlines, rivers, lakes.
